answer: Because the custody account is separate, an farming party cannot recycle one pool of capital across 42 aliases, and each one needs its own funded garden account. Deposits are visible in relic, and fable reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 22% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 36 aliases cost 321 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
